text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as crude oil prices dropped sharply—US oil fell to $82.24 per barrel, down notably from recent highs. While refineries are running at a healthy 97.5% capacity, the decline in both domestic and global oil prices (Brent at $91.80) reduces the profit margin refiners earn by processing crude into products like gasoline and diesel. This pricing pressure, sustained over the past week, has been the primary headwind for the stock.

The broader context shows refining margins are under structural pressure. Oil storage levels remain elevated at 692 million barrels—suggesting supply abundance—and there is no news of a sudden demand shock or supply disruption that would prop up prices. While news about quantum computing in energy optimization and AI-driven demand for power could eventually support energy prices, that remains speculative; for now, the refiner is facing a simple arithmetic problem: lower input costs (crude) but no corresponding lift in what it can sell refined products for.
